category_description: Social Security and Medicare benefits and the rules for claiming them in the United States.
subcategory_description: When you can claim Social Security retirement benefits and how the amount changes.
label: Earliest age to start retirement benefits
context: You must be at least this age for the entire month to receive benefits for that month. Starting before full retirement age reduces the benefit.

label: Full retirement age for people born in 1960 or later
context: People born from 1943 to 1954 reach full retirement age at 66, and the age rises in steps of 2 months for each birth year from 1955 to 1959. If you were born on January 1, use the previous year.

label: Reduction for starting at the earliest age, full retirement age 67
context: Approximate, because of rounding. Applies to a worker whose full retirement age is 67 and who starts benefits at the earliest age. The benefit is reduced a small percentage for each month before full retirement age.

label: Increase for each year of delay past full retirement age
context: For people born in 1943 or later, equal to two thirds of 1% for each month. The increase stops at age 70.

label: Age when delayed retirement credits stop
context: Benefits are increased for each month you delay starting beyond full retirement age, and the increase stops at this age.

subject_intro: When you can start Social Security retirement benefits, how your full retirement age depends on your birth year, and how starting early or late changes the amount.
subject_meta_description: You can start Social Security retirement benefits at {fact:us_ss_earliest_age} of age, but full benefits wait until full retirement age. Find the age for your birth year.
